results.label: this tree ships the M13/M65 calendar ruler (src/periods.js) (the committed parent does not, and that absence is this probe's control)
the ruler is a leaf: it requires nothing, so it cannot inherit a schema or a clock from anywhere
Monday-start weeks: every day of one week resolves to the same Monday, and the next Monday opens the next week
the week is half-open and whole: [Monday, next Monday) with last_day the Sunday before it
a week that crosses a year boundary is still one week and still Monday-start, and its prior week is adjacent
quarters are calendar quarters: the start is the first of Jan/Apr/Jul/Oct and the prior quarter is adjacent
months and years are whole calendars too, February 29 included
every period states its own calendar basis, so a bucket cannot be read on an unstated clock
a period is addressed by its canonical start only: a mid-week or mid-quarter address is refused, never rounded
a day that is not a real calendar day is refused rather than parsed into a nearby one
the bucket key is the period symbol, and a quarter key is the shape a reader can address back
a sequence is the canonical periods ending at the asked-for period, newest first, each one whole
a sequence is bounded rather than unbounded, so a caller cannot ask for a window it cannot read
the review module re-exports the SAME ruler, so a review period and a bucket cannot be computed twice
the review module keeps its OWN error code and wording, so the contract its routes and probes use is unchanged
the quarterly rule-change advisory agrees with the ruler on every day of three years — measured, not assumed
the series bucket on the REVIEW calendar: a UTC close-day decides the week, not the trade order
a bucket is a whole period with its own range, its own trade count, its own days and its own win rate
a close with no recorded amount is NOT a zero: the bucket reports no recorded amount and counts the close
a close with no clock at all is skipped by the series rather than guessed into a week
quarters roll over on the calendar quarter, and a bucket never spans two of them
the buckets are ordered oldest first, so a reader can read a period series without re-sorting it
an empty series is an empty object, never a zero-filled calendar of periods nothing happened in
two rulers, both labelled, and neither converts a trade into the other: the same instant is a different week on the journal clock
a period with no saved artifact is `not_recorded`, with the meaning spelled out — not "missed", not a clean record
the period still running is counted as open rather than as a period that was not reviewed
a saved artifact is joined by its canonical period start and reported as `completed` with its own receipt
a draft is a draft: it is never counted as a completed review
an imported copy is labelled unverified and is never counted as the trader’s own completed review
an unreadable artifact row is reported as unavailable rather than as a period with no review
the LATEST saved version of a period is the one reported, the way the review module reads its own history
another account’s artifact and another owner’s row are not joined into this record
an artifact whose stored start is not a canonical period start is COUNTED as outside the window rather than silently invisible
the recorded amounts are the period’s own: a week with two closes reports them, a week with none reports no amount
a bucket is joined by its own `start`, so a QUARTER bucket — whose key is `2026-Q4`, not a date — still reaches its period
quarterly coverage is the same arithmetic on the quarterly ruler, over its own window
the record is read-only and states what it does not do: no write, no grade/cap/permission influence, no reviewed-vs-unreviewed comparison
an unreadable record is UNKNOWN, never a period list full of "not reviewed"
sampling the pure record against the shipped routes’ error contract: a bad owner or account is refused, not defaulted

scope: M13/M65 pure: the review calendar, its series and the artifact record: actual runtime/auth/SQL/HTTP with a frozen UTC clock, a synthetic calendar fed through the app's own parser and a patched market module for the thrown-read path; M111 calendar-read states (blocked/clear/unknown), no provider/broker/pixel/human proof and no claim about what a release does to price
